source_text: Qui inter cetera salutaria sua monita et praecepta diuina quibus populo suo consulit ad salutem etiam orandi ipse formam dedit, ipse quid precaremur monuit et instruxit. qui fecit uiuere docuit et orare, benignitate ea scilicet qua et cetera dare et conferre dignatus est, ut dum prece et oratione quam filius docuit aput patrem loquimur, facilius audiamur. iam praedixerat horam uenire, quando ueri adoratores adorarent patrem in spiritu et ueritate, et inpleuit quod ante promisit, ut qui spiritum et ueritatem de eius sanctificatione percepimus de traditione quoque eius uere et spiritaliter adoremus. quae enim potest esse spiritalis oratio quam quae a Christo nobis data est, a quo nobis et Spiritus sanctus missus est, quae uera aput patrem precatio quam quae a filio qui est ueritas de eius ore prolata est? ut aliter orare quam docuit non ignorantia sola sit sed et culpa,; quando ipse posuerit et dixerit: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis.
thought_title: Christ gave the form of prayer
orientation: Cyprian is explaining that Christ, among his saving commands, himself gave the form and words of prayer so that Christians may be heard by the Father.
pass_a_gloss: Who among [the] other salutary his warnings and precepts divine by which [to] people his he consults [for] salvation also [of] praying himself [the] form gave, himself what we should pray [for] warned and instructed. [he] who made [to] live taught also [to] pray, [by] kindness that namely by which also [the] other things to give and to bestow he deemed worthy, so that while [by] prayer and supplication which [the] son taught before [the] father we speak, more easily we may be heard. already he had foretold [the] hour to come, when true worshippers would worship [the] father in spirit and truth, and he fulfilled what before he promised, so that [we] who [the] spirit and truth from his sanctification have received from [the] tradition also of him truly and spiritually may worship. what indeed can be spiritual prayer than that which by Christ to us has been given, by whom to us also [the] Holy Spirit has been sent, what true before [the] father supplication than that which by [the] son who is [the] truth from his mouth has been brought forth? so that to pray otherwise than he taught not ignorance alone may be but also fault, when he himself has set down and said: you reject [the] commandment of God, so that your tradition you may establish.

choices.why: Keeps the literal noun 'formam' as 'form' and the gerund 'orandi' as 'of praying', matching the source's emphasis on Christ giving a pattern.
The subjunctive 'precaremur' is an indirect question; 'should' preserves the deliberative force.
'scilicet' is rendered as 'clearly' to keep its explanatory force without smoothing it away.
The preposition 'de' is kept as 'from' to preserve the source's spatial metaphor of receiving spirit and truth from Christ's sanctifying work.

choices.english: has been brought forth from the mouth of the Son
choices.why: 'prolata est' is passive perfect; 'brought forth' keeps the image of the Son's mouth as the source of the true prayer.

choices.term: non ignorantia sola sit sed et culpa
choices.english: is not only ignorance but also fault
choices.why: The correlative 'sola...sed et' is kept literally as 'not only...but also' to preserve the sharp contrast.
rejected: is not merely ignorance but guilt

bible_refs.note: quoted source words: horam uenire, quando ueri adoratores adorarent patrem in spiritu et ueritate
quoted source words: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis

pass_b_english: Among the rest of his saving warnings and divine precepts by which he provides for his people's salvation, he also gave us the form of praying himself; he himself taught and instructed us what we should pray for. He who made us live also taught us to pray, with that same kindness by which he deigned to give and bestow all other things, so that when we speak to the Father in the prayer and petition the Son taught, we may be heard more easily. He had already foretold that the hour was coming when true worshippers would worship the Father in spirit and truth, and he fulfilled what he promised before, so that we who have received spirit and truth from his sanctification may also worship truly and spiritually according to his teaching. For what prayer can be spiritual except the one given to us by Christ, from whom the Holy Spirit was also sent to us? What true petition before the Father can there be except the one brought forth from the mouth of the Son, who is truth? So to pray otherwise than he taught is not only ignorance but also fault, since he himself declared and said: “You reject the commandment of God, to establish your own tradition” (Mark 7:9).

last_rejected.why: Latin 'statuatis' means 'set up/establish' but context demands 'in place of' or 'at expense of' God's command; 'to establish' alone misses the replacement sense.
last_rejected.fix: to set your own tradition in place of God's command
last_rejected.ruling: 'statuatis' means 'establish/set up'; the replacement sense is carried by 'ut', not the verb itself. Standard rendering.

last_rejected.source_quote: reicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem uestram statuatis
last_rejected.why: The quotation matches Mark 7:8-9, but Cyprian's exact wording closer to Matthew 15:3 or Mark 7:9; however, the citation should note the conflated tradition.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'reicitis mandatum Dei' matches Mark 7:9 exactly. Citation is correct; no conflated tradition issue.
